basic_identification.name: Latent space exploration
basic_identification.originator: Key practitioners: Holly Herndon and Mat Dryhurst (artificial psychedelia, spawning, readyweights, protocol art), Mario Klingemann (neurography, GAN exploration), Sofia Crespo (biological latent space), Refik Anadol (data painting through model navigation). Academic: The Canon of Latent Spaces project (University of Zurich). Tools: Midjourney, ComfyUI, Stable Diffusion ecosystem.
basic_identification.geography: Global. Berlin (Herndon/Dryhurst, Klingemann), worldwide online practice. The practice is internet-native and not geographically concentrated. Academic centers in Zurich, London, New York.

core_ideas.core_claim: Working within AI model embedding spaces constitutes a distinct artistic practice. The latent space -- the high-dimensional mathematical representation of concepts learned by AI models -- is a new territory for artistic exploration. Artists navigate, probe, and manipulate this space as a creative medium. Prompt engineering is an aesthetic practice, not merely a technical skill. The artist becomes a navigator of compressed cultural possibility space.
core_ideas.medium_specificity: Maximally digitally native. The medium does not exist outside of computation. Latent spaces are mathematical abstractions (high-dimensional vector spaces) that can only be navigated through computational tools. The aesthetic is specific to model architecture: GANs produce different latent space topologies than diffusion models than transformers. The practice is native to the era of large foundation models and could not have existed before deep learning.
core_ideas.relation_to_attention_economy: Ambivalent. Midjourney (the most accessible latent space tool) is a $300M+/year business built on attention-economy dynamics (easy prompting, shareable outputs). The mass adoption of text-to-image tools has created an enormous attention surface for latent space aesthetics. But serious practitioners distinguish their work from casual prompt-and-share. Herndon/Dryhurst's conceptual exploration of embeddings operates in a different register than Instagram AI art. The tension between accessible spectacle and deep practice is defining.
core_ideas.relation_to_intention: Split. Herndon/Dryhurst's work is deeply intention-native: they interrogate the political economy of latent spaces, develop consent frameworks, and propose new IP models (the readyweight). Academic research (Canon of Latent Spaces) serves field knowledge. But the mass of prompt-engineering practice is attention-native: optimizing for striking outputs shareable on social media. The practice contains both its most intention-native and its most attention-native practitioners.

market_economics.revenue_model: Diverse. Midjourney: subscription model ($300M+ ARR). Artist NFT sales (Herndon/Dryhurst readyweights on Zora). Gallery representation and institutional commissions. Tool development and commercial licensing. Academic research grants. The practice generates economic value at both the tool layer (Midjourney, ComfyUI) and the art layer (individual practitioners).
market_economics.market_position: Spans the entire market: infrastructure (Midjourney, ComfyUI), primary market (artist sales, NFTs), institutional (museum exhibitions, biennials). The Whitney Biennial inclusion of Herndon/Dryhurst (2024) signals top-tier institutional positioning. Midjourney occupies the mass-market tool position.
market_economics.price_range: Enormous range reflecting the practice's breadth. Herndon/Dryhurst conceptual works: $5K-$50K+. Klingemann gallery works: $10K-$100K. Mass AI art: $1-$100. Midjourney subscription: $10-$60/month. The market ranges from high-art institutional to mass-consumer. [uncertain]
market_economics.volume_trend_2024_2026: Growing explosively at the tool level (millions of Midjourney/Stable Diffusion users). Growing at the institutional art level (Whitney Biennial, KW Berlin, major galleries). The sheer volume of AI-generated imagery is unprecedented. But serious latent-space art practice (as distinct from casual image generation) is a small, growing subset. The challenge is signal-to-noise: distinguishing artistic practice from mass production.
market_economics.collector_demographics: At the art level: contemporary art collectors, crypto-native collectors, tech industry collectors. At the tool level: millions of casual users worldwide. The gap between these demographics is enormous -- casual Midjourney users and Whitney Biennial attendees are almost entirely separate populations. [uncertain]
market_economics.sustainability: Strong at the tool level (Midjourney profitable, open-source tools thriving). Uncertain at the art level -- the practice depends on continued AI model development and on establishing aesthetic criteria that distinguish artistic practice from mass generation. If AI-generated imagery becomes fully commoditized, the artistic premium may evaporate. Herndon/Dryhurst's conceptual framing provides more durable value than purely visual practice.

practice_aesthetics.toolchain: Midjourney (text-to-image), Stable Diffusion (open-source diffusion), ComfyUI (node-based workflow), DALL-E (OpenAI), custom model training (DreamBooth, LoRA fine-tuning), Runway (video), embedding visualization tools, prompt engineering tools. Python/PyTorch for custom work. Herndon/Dryhurst use custom embedding exploration tools. Klingemann uses custom GAN architectures.
practice_aesthetics.relation_to_AI: AI is the medium itself. The practice is defined by its relationship to AI -- specifically to the internal representations (latent spaces, embeddings) of AI models. This is not AI-as-tool but AI-as-territory to be explored. The practice makes the hidden computational substrate of AI visible and navigable. Different model architectures constitute different territories with different topographies.
practice_aesthetics.liveness: Primarily generative (each prompt/navigation produces new outputs). Some works are static artifacts (selected outputs). The interactive process of navigating latent space is inherently real-time and exploratory. Herndon/Dryhurst's xhairymutantx at the Whitney Biennial was an evolving installation. ComfyUI workflows enable real-time generative exploration.
practice_aesthetics.aesthetic_vocabulary: Rapidly developing. Key terms: latent space, embedding, prompt engineering, diffusion, denoising, classifier-free guidance, LoRA, fine-tuning, interpolation, latent walk, style transfer, artificial psychedelia (Herndon/Dryhurst), spawning, readyweight, the latent camera (Dryhurst), catness (compressed concept), model collapse, hallucination, surface aesthetics. Academic: Canon of Latent Spaces, compressed probability fields. The vocabulary is rich but unstable -- new model architectures introduce new terms and new aesthetic possibilities faster than criticism can process.
practice_aesthetics.tendency_axis_position: Diverse. The tool layer (Midjourney) is commercially enclosed. The open-source layer (Stable Diffusion, ComfyUI) is commons. The art layer spans individual (artist-brand) to collective (open-source community). The practice as a whole is more spectacle (visual output) than infrastructure (conceptual framework), except at the Herndon/Dryhurst end.

infrastructure_governance.openness: Split. Stable Diffusion, ComfyUI: fully open-source. Midjourney: proprietary, closed-source. DALL-E: proprietary API. Custom artist tools: generally proprietary. Model weights: varies (some open, some closed). The practice exists across the full openness spectrum. The open-source ecosystem is vibrant and growing.
infrastructure_governance.governance_model: No collective governance of the practice. Midjourney: corporate. Stable Diffusion: Stability AI corporate with community forks. ComfyUI: open-source community. Academic projects: university governance. Individual artists: autonomous. No DAO or field-wide governance mechanism.
infrastructure_governance.data_sovereignty: Central contested issue. Training data sovereignty is the defining political question: who controls the data that creates the latent space? Herndon/Dryhurst's Spawning project (haveibeentrained.com) gives artists tools to check and control their data presence. Model providers control the latent spaces. Users generally do not own or control the models they use. Generated outputs ownership is legally unclear.
infrastructure_governance.interoperability: Moderate. Standard image formats for outputs. Model formats (safetensors, ONNX) enable some interoperability. ComfyUI workflows are shareable. But latent spaces themselves are model-specific and not interoperable. No standard for documenting the provenance of AI-generated art (which model, which prompt, which seed, which fine-tuning data).
infrastructure_governance.preservation_strategy: Weak. Generated images can be preserved normally. But the generative process (specific model version, specific weights, specific prompt, specific parameters) is rarely documented or preserved. If a model version becomes unavailable, the exact outputs cannot be reproduced. No systematic preservation framework for latent space art. This is a critical gap.
infrastructure_governance.consent_architecture: Emerging. Spawning's opt-in/opt-out for training data is the most advanced consent infrastructure. Stability AI nominally supports opt-out via LAION exclusion. Most model providers offer limited or no consent mechanisms. The EU AI Act and various national regulations are pushing toward consent requirements. Machine-readable consent standards (C2PA, Spawning's protocol) are emerging but not yet standard.

field_position.relation_to_traditional_art_world: Accelerating integration. Whitney Biennial 2024 (Herndon/Dryhurst). KW Berlin 2025 (Starmirror). Major galleries representing AI artists. Sotheby's and Christie's AI art sales. The traditional art world is actively engaging with latent space art, though critical frameworks are lagging behind market and institutional interest.
field_position.what_it_enables: A genuinely new artistic medium (navigating compressed cultural possibility space). Democratized image creation (anyone with a prompt can generate). New forms of authorship (orchestrating AI systems rather than directly producing). New IP models (readyweights, embeddings as property). Critical investigation of how AI encodes and reproduces culture. Public engagement with AI's internal representations.
field_position.what_it_lacks: Critical vocabulary adequate to the pace of change. Standards for documenting AI art provenance. Consent frameworks universally adopted. Preservation strategies for the generative process. Criteria for distinguishing artistic practice from casual generation. A critical discourse that goes beyond novelty and addresses the aesthetic and cultural implications in depth.
field_position.who_is_excluded: Those without access to computational resources (GPUs, cloud compute). Non-English speakers (prompting is predominantly in English, and models encode English-language cultural biases). Artists from underrepresented cultures whose aesthetics are underrepresented in training data. Those without technical literacy to navigate AI tools. The visually impaired (the practice is overwhelmingly visual). [uncertain]
field_position.frontier_signal: Frontier and accelerating. New model architectures (video generation, 3D, multi-modal) continuously create new latent spaces to explore. The practice is expanding faster than critical or institutional frameworks can accommodate. The readyweight concept (Herndon/Dryhurst) represents a conceptual frontier. Academic research (Canon of Latent Spaces) represents a critical frontier.

attention_intention.discovery_mechanism: Social media (Twitter/X, Instagram, Reddit -- AI art is extremely viral), Midjourney community (Discord), institutional exhibitions, academic conferences, word of mouth, YouTube tutorials. The mass-adoption tools (Midjourney) have their own discovery ecosystems. The art-world tier uses institutional channels.
attention_intention.attention_dependency: High at the mass level (AI image generation thrives on social media sharing). Moderate at the institutional art level (institutional exhibition provides some attention-independence). The practice's identity is entangled with AI hype cycles. If public interest in AI wanes, the mass practice contracts but the serious art practice may benefit from reduced noise.
attention_intention.intention_alignment: Split. Herndon/Dryhurst: strongly intention-native (interrogating the medium, building consent infrastructure, proposing new IP models). Canon of Latent Spaces: intention-native (academic knowledge production). Mass prompt engineering: attention-native (generating striking images for social sharing). The practice contains both extremes. A(DAI) should focus on the intention-native strand.
attention_intention.commons_contribution: Growing. Open-source models (Stable Diffusion) are a massive commons contribution. ComfyUI workflows are shared freely. Academic research on latent spaces is published. Herndon/Dryhurst's conceptual frameworks (spawning, readyweight, latent camera) are public intellectual contributions. Spawning's tools are open access. However, commercial tools (Midjourney) enclose their contributions.

provenance_temporality.provenance_type: Weak. The most important provenance information for latent space art -- which model, which training data, which prompt, which parameters, which fine-tuning -- is rarely systematically recorded. Herndon/Dryhurst's readyweight concept begins to address this by linking generated output to its location in the model's latent space. C2PA metadata standard is emerging for AI-generated content but adoption is early.
provenance_temporality.temporal_logic: Real-time (generative exploration), anticipatory (the practice constantly points toward next-generation models), archival (outputs are preserved as files). The temporal experience of navigating latent space is distinctly non-linear -- moving through compressed cultural possibility rather than through time.
provenance_temporality.absence_handling: The practice implicitly addresses absence through what models fail to represent. The Canon of Latent Spaces project explores how models encode dominant perspectives and erase marginal ones. The concept of model bias reveals what is absent from the training data. Herndon/Dryhurst's work on data consent highlights absent consent frameworks.

coherence.coherence_vs_consensus: Coherence without consensus. The practice encompasses wildly different approaches: Herndon/Dryhurst's conceptual protocol art, Klingemann's GAN neurography, Crespo's biological latent spaces, mass Midjourney generation. No authority defines what latent space art is. Multiple valid practices coexist under a loose umbrella.
coherence.contestability: Very high. Everything is contested: is prompt engineering art? Does the prompter have authorship? Is AI-generated imagery original? Who owns the outputs? Should training data require consent? The practice exists in a state of productive contestation on aesthetic, legal, and ethical fronts.
coherence.forkability: Very high. Open-source models can be forked, fine-tuned, and modified. Prompt engineering techniques are freely shared. The conceptual frameworks (spawning, readyweight) are publicly available. Commercial tools (Midjourney) cannot be forked but open-source alternatives exist. The practice is highly forkable both technically and conceptually.

adai_comparison.what_adai_should_adopt: Herndon/Dryhurst's consent architecture (Spawning, opt-in/opt-out) as a model for A(DAI)'s consent layer. The readyweight concept as a new form of provenance linking output to its position in model space. The latent camera metaphor as a way of understanding AI as a new perceptual technology. The Canon of Latent Spaces' approach to analyzing cultural bias in model representations. The open-source ecosystem's commons ethic.
adai_comparison.what_adai_should_refuse: The attention-native mass generation that treats AI as a content mill. The lack of provenance standards for AI-generated art. The commercial enclosure of latent spaces by proprietary model providers. The visual-output-only focus that ignores the conceptual and political dimensions of working with AI models. The hype-cycle dependency.
adai_comparison.structural_tension: Latent space exploration reveals that AI models contain compressed, navigable representations of culture. A(DAI) must decide how to relate to this: is latent space a territory to be mapped, a medium to be classified, or a meta-layer that contains representations of everything A(DAI) might track? The tension is between treating latent space art as one practice among many and recognizing that AI latent spaces may become the substrate on which all digital cultural production occurs.

regulatory_legal.regulatory_exposure: High and rapidly evolving. EU AI Act requirements for AI-generated content disclosure. AB 2013 (California) labeling requirements. Copyright disputes over training data (Stability AI lawsuits). US Copyright Office requires disclosure of AI involvement for registration. DMCA implications for AI-generated derivatives. C2PA metadata standard being developed for provenance. This is the most legally contested area in digital art.
regulatory_legal.ip_model: Deeply contested. US Copyright Office: AI-generated works may not be copyrightable without sufficient human authorship. Generated outputs: unclear ownership. Training data: contested (fair use vs. copyright infringement). Herndon/Dryhurst's readyweight proposes new IP based on embeddings. Model weights: proprietary (for commercial models) or open (for open-source). No consensus on any aspect of IP.
regulatory_legal.opt_in_vs_opt_out: Currently opt-out for training data (artists must actively exclude themselves). Regulatory pressure moving toward opt-in (EU AI Act). Spawning provides opt-out tools. Midjourney and others offer limited opt-out mechanisms. The shift from opt-out to opt-in is the most significant regulatory change on the horizon for this practice.

ecosystem.platform_dependency: High dependency on model providers: OpenAI (DALL-E), Stability AI (Stable Diffusion), Midjourney, Google (Imagen). GPU cloud providers (AWS, Google Cloud, Lambda). Open-source models reduce but do not eliminate dependency. The practice depends on continued AI model development by large companies. ComfyUI and other tools provide some independence at the workflow level.
ecosystem.network_effects: Very strong. Larger models trained on more data produce richer latent spaces. More users generate more fine-tuning data and prompt techniques. Open-source community contributions improve tools and models. The practice benefits from the massive network effects of the broader AI ecosystem. However, commercial capture (Midjourney's closed ecosystem) can redirect these network effects away from the commons.
ecosystem.post_crash_trajectory: Accelerating through the crash. Unlike NFT-dependent practices, latent space exploration has grown dramatically since 2022 as AI models improved. The NFT crash is irrelevant to this practice's trajectory. The driving force is technological capability, not market speculation. Institutional recognition (Whitney Biennial 2024, major galleries) has grown alongside tool adoption. The practice is on a strong upward trajectory.
